enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / Can't tell: no longitudinal household cohort was empirically followed (outcomes are ex-ante projections), and participant retention or response rates across the conference panel, web survey, and 30-day/15-day focus group stages are not reported (PDF pp. 2, 6).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern: baseline projections rely on bivariate linear time trends (Equation 1, PDF p. 4) without controlling for household socioeconomic status, tariff elasticity, peripheral urban informality, or municipal enforcement capacity, and policy impacts are simulated ex ante without an empirical comparator.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Adequate to strong: accurately identifies Federal Law no. 11445/2007 (art. 45), Minas Gerais State Law no. 13317/1999 (art. 48), and State Law no. 18309/2009, and precisely distinguishes municipal enforcement authority over mandatory household connections from ARSAE's tariff-design jurisdiction, though the specific regulatory rules underlying scenarios A1-A3 remain schematic (PDF pp. 1-3, 10).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: High concern: outcome values across policy options (non-connected households, hospital stays/year, tariff revenues, infrastructure capex/opex, and sludge load) are ex-ante model projections combined with subjective stakeholder MACBETH value scores rather than observed empirical measurements, with inconsistent time horizons reported between text (2016-2023, PDF p. 4) and Table 1 (2017-2026, PDF p. 6).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak: all five sanitation, health, economic, and environmental outcomes in Table 1 are hypothetical ex-ante forecasts rather than empirically measured post-intervention outcomes, and operational definitions, baseline data series, and projection equations for individual indicators are largely relegated to online appendices (PDF pp. 4-6).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern: no pre-specified protocol is reported; essential model inputs, baseline regressions, value functions, and cost-benefit derivations are deferred to online Appendices 1-6; and internal reporting inconsistencies appear across the text (e.g., 2016-2023 on PDF p. 4 vs 2017-2026 in Table 1 on PDF p. 6; A2 called 'advanced infrastructure diffusion' on PDF pp. 4, 9 but 'intermediate infrastructure diffusion' in the Conclusion on PDF p. 10).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern: the four BBCR municipalities were purposively chosen without a formal sampling frame, and stakeholder recruitment for the focus group, conference panel, and web survey lacks sample sizes, eligibility criteria, or response rates, with the authors noting that environmental and water-resource entities were omitted (PDF pp. 2, 3, 10).

domain_ratings.justification: Accurately cites primary Brazilian federal and state statutes governing mandatory wastewater connections and regulatory jurisdiction—specifically Federal Law no. 11445/2007 (art. 45), Minas Gerais State Law no. 13317/1999 (art. 48), and Minas Gerais State Law no. 18309/2009 establishing ARSAE—and correctly states the division of legal competence between municipalities and the state regulator.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1-3 (Introduction; Water and Wastewater Services: Brazil)

domain_ratings.justification: Clearly bounds the institutional and geographic scope to Brazil, the State of Minas Gerais, utilities regulated by ARSAE (COPASA, COPANOR, and municipal providers), and the four case-study municipalities of Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirao das Neves (BBCR), explicitly warning against uncritical generalization to other jurisdictions.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 2-3, 9-10 (Water and Wastewater Services: Brazil; Methodology - Status quo; Path Forward; Conclusion)

domain_ratings.justification: Defines four prospective regulatory policy options in terms of target percentage reductions in the non-connected household gap (A1: 100%, A2: 75%, A3: 50%, A4/Do nothing: 0%), grounded in ARSAE tariff-mechanism incentives, but leaves the concrete regulatory/tariff instrument design schematic in the main text (deferring details to online Appendix 1) and mislabels A2 in the Conclusion.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 3-4, 6, 10 (Methodology - Status quo; Table 1; Conclusion)

domain_ratings.justification: Identifies five criteria across social (CSo1 non-connected households; CSo2 hospital stay/year), economic (CEc1 average tariffs/revenues; Infra capex and opex), and environmental (CEn1 sludge kg/year) dimensions, but main-text definitions of units, exact denominators, and time horizons are imprecise and inconsistent (2016-2023 in text vs 2017-2026 in Table 1).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 4-6 (Methodology - Status quo; Results Achieved - Table 1)

domain_ratings.justification: Provides no participant counts, organizational breakdown, or response rates for the stakeholder focus group, conference panel, or web survey, describing respondents only generally as ARSAE staff, academics, and local government members regarded as regional/local experts.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 2, 3, 5 (Introduction; Methodology - Status quo; Consultation: focus group)

domain_ratings.justification: Does not explain how individual experts or web-survey participants were selected or invited, nor why only four municipalities (BBCR) were chosen from ARSAE's ~3.5 million regulated households; the authors explicitly acknowledge that environmental and water-resource entities were not included in the focus group.

Presents the general linear projection formula (Equations 1-3, curiously specifying a Student t-distribution with 2 degrees of freedom in Equation 3) and MACBETH aggregation (Equation 4), but omits underlying historical data series, parameter estimates, exact cost-benefit derivations for the BRL 33M cost and BRL 42M surplus figures, and value functions for four of the five criteria (relegated to online Appendices 1-6).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1, 4-8, 10 (Abstract; Methodology; Results Achieved; Conclusion)

domain_ratings.justification: No empirical causal identification strategy is present; the study is an ex-ante regulatory impact assessment that projects hypothetical scenario outcomes via linear trends and evaluates them through stakeholder preference weights rather than observing actual regulatory implementation or counterfactual household behavior.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1, 4-6, 10 (Abstract; Methodology - Status quo; Results Achieved; Conclusion)

domain_ratings.justification: Bivariate linear time-trend projections and deterministic scenario targets do not adjust for household socioeconomic, behavioral, spatial, or municipal enforcement confounders; sensitivity and robustness analyses test MCDA criterion weights and score uncertainty rather than empirical confounding.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 4, 8 (Methodology - Status quo; Results Achieved - Additional analysis)

domain_ratings.justification: Provides a clear, well-contextualized analysis of Brazil's decentralized municipal sanitation structure, the post-1997 emergence of 50 subnational water regulators, COPASA/COPANOR utility operations, household tariff-avoidance behavior, and the statutory mismatch between municipal inspection powers and state tariff regulation.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1-3, 8, 10 (Introduction; Water and Wastewater Services: Brazil; Policy options; Path Forward)

domain_ratings.justification: Independent replication is severely constrained because raw municipal baseline series, MATLAB projection inputs, web-survey questionnaires, stakeholder composition, and Appendices 1-6 details are unavailable in the main text, and M-MACBETH value functions rely on unrecorded interactive focus-group consensus.

Describes the three-stage MACBETH consultation workflow (structuring issues, ordinal-to-cardinal scale transition over 30 days, and swing-weighting matrix validation over 15 days), but provides no coding protocol, survey instrument, or rules for resolving inter-stakeholder disagreement into consensus weights.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 5-7 (Consultation: focus group; Structuring issues and scale transition; Weighting coefficients)

domain_ratings.justification: Although the authors candidly note that excluding environmental and water-resource entities from the focus group could influence criterion weights, they do not address researcher positionality or potential institutional bias arising from co-author affiliation with ARSAE (the regulatory agency whose intervention is being designed and promoted).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF pp. 1, 2, 10 (Author affiliations; Introduction; Path Forward)

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Structured non-validated appraisal using the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework: de Carvalho et al. (2019) present an ex-ante Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) case study of household wastewater connection policy in four municipalities of Minas Gerais, Brazil (Belo Horizonte, Betim, Contagem, and Ribeirao das Neves), regulated by ARSAE. The study exhibits strong legal source accuracy, jurisdictional specificity, and institutional contextualization—accurately detailing Federal Law no. 11445/2007 (art. 45), State Law no. 13317/1999 (art. 48), and State Law no. 18309/2009, and explaining why ARSAE cannot directly inspect or sanction non-connected households (a municipal power) and must instead act via tariff incentives. However, as empirical evidence on regulatory effectiveness, the study has substantial methodological limitations: all policy impacts (75% connection-gap reduction, BRL 33 million expenditure, BRL 42 million revenue surplus, 17,414 tons less sludge, and 12.5% waterborne disease avoidance) are ex-ante projections rather than observed ex-post outcomes; baseline linear projections (apparently using very few observations, given 2 degrees of freedom in Equation 3) omit household and municipal confounders; focus-group, conference-panel, and web-survey sample sizes and selection procedures are unreported (and exclude environmental/water-resource entities); co-author affiliation with ARSAE is not reflexively examined in relation to preference weighting; and core data, value functions, and cost-benefit derivations are deferred to online appendices alongside minor timeframe and option-label inconsistencies in the main text.
raw_response.overall_rating: Structured non-validated judgment: High methodological concern for empirical impact inference (strong legal-institutional contextualization; weak sampling transparency, measurement transparency, confounding control, and causal identification due to ex-ante MCDA projection design)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) institutional case study combining statutory/governance analysis, stakeholder multi-criteria decision analysis (MACBETH focus group, conference panel, and web survey), linear baseline trend projection, and cost-benefit analysis
raw_response.where_found_summary: Study design and stakeholder/MCDA methods: Abstract (PDF p. 1), Introduction (PDF p. 2), and Methodology (PDF pp. 3-5). Legal and institutional analysis of Brazilian sanitation laws and ARSAE mandates: Introduction and Water and Wastewater Services: Brazil (PDF pp. 1-3). Projections, policy option scores, sensitivity/robustness, and cost-benefit results: Results Achieved (PDF pp. 5-8, Table 1, Figures 2-5). Scope limitations, missing stakeholder groups, and ex-ante framing: Path Forward and Conclusion (PDF pp. 9-10).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: S937 is an ex-ante regulatory impact assessment (RIA) and institutional/statutory case study evaluating four hypothetical regulatory options for household wastewater connections in Minas Gerais using statutory mandate analysis, municipal gap data, linear trend projections, and stakeholder M-MACBETH preference elicitation (focus group, conference panel, and web survey). Because no regulatory intervention was empirically implemented or observed ex post, ROBINS-I and JBI observational checklists do not apply; because stakeholder consultation was used strictly to construct numerical MCDA value functions and weights rather than conduct qualitative thematic inquiry or mixed-methods empirical integration, CASP and MMAT do not fit; and unlike a purely abstract mathematical model with no institutional or stakeholder data (NONE), this doctrinal-institutional regulatory case study is directly suited to the 13-domain Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework.
